_comment: Copy to config/candidate.json and fill in. This file drives everything: which jobs are collected, which are eligible, and what the tailored resume may claim.

identity.name: Your Name
identity.workAuthorization: Where you can legally work, and whether you need sponsorship. Be accurate — this decides which jobs are reachable.

eligibility._comment: THE master switch. 'global-only' means a job must be open to candidates anywhere, with no country restriction. 'global-plus-india' also accepts roles explicitly open to India/APAC.
eligibility._modeEvidence: Set to global-only on the owner's instruction: he wants roles he can do from anywhere, full stop. The cost is real - the first measurement of this setting found 1 eligible job in 12,192. The answer is not to loosen the filter but to search far more thoroughly, which is why the sources now paginate deeply instead of taking the first page. Set to global-plus-india to also see India-tied roles.

_tracks: A job is classified into exactly one track before anything else happens. The track decides the salary band, the seniority rule, which resume facts get selected, and how the dashboard groups it. Turn a track off with enabled:false and it stops being collected entirely.

marketing.label: Media Buying / Paid Ads
marketing._salaryMin: Lower floor than the dev tracks on purpose. Global-remote paid-media roles routinely pay below $50k, and a $50k floor would reject the entire track before he saw any of it.

game.label: Game Development
game._entryOnly: He described himself as a beginner here. Anything above junior is filtered out, because a mid-level game role would waste a researched dossier and a recorded Loom.

_excludeTitles: Hard exclusions, checked BEFORE track matching. These are the shapes of job that filled v1's results and that he has no interest in or background for. A title hitting any of these is dropped even if it also matches a track.

employment._comment: Full-time only, as instructed. Contract, part-time, internship and freelance are rejected at layer 1.

_excludeCompanies: Whole employers whose entire output is the wrong kind of work. Canonical is here because you said plainly that you do not know Ubuntu and have no interest in it - their board is Linux systems engineering end to end, and it was filling your results in v1. Delete the entry to let them back in; nothing else depends on it.

seniority._rejectTitlePatterns: Note that 'ads manager' and 'campaign manager' are legitimate individual-contributor marketing titles, so bare 'manager' is NOT rejected - only management-of-people titles are.

compensation._comment: Per-track floors live under tracks. These are the fallbacks for a job whose track could not be resolved, plus the FX table used to compare a non-USD posting against a USD band.

fxToUSD._comment: Your rates, not fetched ones. A filter that silently re-prices itself is a filter you cannot audit.

skills._comment: Used for fit scoring and the ATS keyword check. The resume-tailor may only emphasise what is here - it may never claim a skill that is not. Grows when a resume is uploaded or the gap interview is answered.
skills._unproven: Claimed by the owner but NOT evidenced by any resume on disk. The tailorer must not assert these until the gap interview supplies real detail - see data/resume/master.json.

scoring._comment: Applied only to jobs that already PASSED the eligibility gate. Eligibility is a gate, not a weight - a US-only job cannot be scored into contention.
